name: How do undermount, drop-in, and vessel sinks compare for new countertops?

mainEntity.name: How do undermount, drop-in, and vessel sinks compare for new countertops?

acceptedAnswer.text: Undermount sinks mount beneath the countertop for a sleek profile and easy counter wipe-downs, but they require polished internal cutouts and professional adhesive brackets. Drop-in sinks sit on top of the counter cutout with a raised rim; they are simpler to install and replace later, but the perimeter lip collects grime over time. Vessel sinks rest on top of the counter surface, offering a dramatic accent, though they require a lower vanity height and tall faucets. Your choice impacts how the stone fabricator cuts your slab and how your supply lines are configured.
acceptedAnswer.description: Undermount sinks allow easy wipe-downs but cost more in slab cutting. Drop-in sinks install easily but have raised rims. Vessel sinks create a bold look but alter faucet height.
